text:
Vince Dunn plays almost 23 minutes a night for Seattle, and a lot of those minutes are spent defending. At five on five the Kraken take only about 39% of the shot attempts and 43% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and they do a bit better without him. Those are rough numbers for a top-pair defenseman.

The production holds up anyway: 3 goals and 11 points in 19 games, five of them on the power play, where he's still Seattle's quarterback. His finishing is about where his chances say it should be.

There's context worth keeping. Evolving-Hockey said last season that his teammates ranked in the bottom 4% by their impact, which drags down his raw on-ice numbers. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows both halves of him: 96th percentile among defensemen for chances from right in front of the net, but only 31% of his exits keep possession. The 2019 Cup winner is an offensive defenseman being asked to do everything. Watch his breakouts against heavy forechecks; that's where the shot share slips away.
